column1: # CEO-1507 (the ceo to the coo, 2026-10-04): the 23 Prolog kernels timed before and after hq_prolog's rewrite -- a SCOUTING DATUM, never a README number.
# BEFORE bc6092368 (2026-10-03 12:56, the tree before the rewrite) · AFTER 74de64bd4 (origin HEAD as built, 2026-10-04) · corpus 29487b519 · RT_OPT -O0 both trees · SCRIP_DIAG=0
# iter_n=3 bud_ms=1000 reps=3 (best of); start 2026-10-04 18:00:00 CDT load 1.51 2.89 4.45 on 16 cores

# ANGLES (the prolog-bench-ref angles, test_prolog_bench_suite.sh): process = the pristine kernel under tools/bench_rusage, best elapsed of 3 (m3 includes its compile); iter = bench_prolog_wrap.sh --mode=iter --n=3, the BENCH work_us, best of 3; time = --mode=time --bud=1000, iterations in the budget, one run. Every run held to <k>.ref (process: stdout == ref; iter: loop_check; time: stdout == ref and mismatched=0); the two trees run interleaved per kernel and mode. Kernel sizes from each kernel's .heap/.stack sidecars.

# x_* = SPEEDUP of AFTER over BEFORE (>1 = faster after): process and iter = before_us/after_us, time = after_iters/before_iters. Lowest-noise angle: time (a 1 s budget); iter at n=3 is a few ms or less per kernel.
